issues.description: `_index_active_standing_decisions(...)` is invoked OUTSIDE the try/except that gives `filter_entity_standing_decisions` its documented fail-open contract ("a ledger read failure must never hide a finding" — the try wraps only `list_entity_standing_decisions`). The amendment materially grew the raise surface of that call: `row.expires_at < now` raises TypeError if `expires_at` is anything but a str (the `recon_ledger` column is TEXT, but SQLite is dynamically typed and `_record_from_row` does no coercion — only α's `upsert_entity_standing_decision` enforces non-None, never str-ness), and `sorted(match.flag_type for match in matches)` in the ambiguity WARNING raises TypeError on a mixed None/str grounds set. Either raise escapes the filter entirely and aborts Stage 1's whole flag chain — a strictly worse outcome than the fail-open path the same function takes for an unreadable ledger, and the opposite of what the new docstring promises ("dropped rather than indexed ... because suppressing on either would hide a finding"). Not blocking: every production writer goes through α, which validates grounds ∈ GROUNDS_ENUM and writes isoformat strings, so neither shape is reachable today.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend the existing `try:` block to cover the index build, e.g. move `active_by_uuid = _index_active_standing_decisions(rows, project_id, now_str)` inside the same try as the ledger read (its `except Exception` already returns the unfiltered pass-through result and logs WARNING with exc_info). That keeps the whole 'read + index' step under one fail-open guard with no new code path, and the existing read-failure test already pins the degradation shape.

issues.description: `test_lapsed_ttl_row_is_skipped_with_info` asserts on the ADJECTIVE in the log line — `'lapsed' in rec.getMessage()`. That word is prose, not behaviour: rewording the INFO message to e.g. 'TTL expired' or 'past expires_at' reddens the test with nothing executable changed, which is exactly the prose-pin shape this repo has been removing from its test suite in recent commits (`stop pinning the complexipy rationale prose`, `stop pinning README prose`). The sibling ambiguity test gets this right — it asserts the entity uuid and both grounds values, all of which are DATA the message must carry and survive a full reword. Note the substantive half of this assertion (`indexed == {}`) is already unconditional above it, so the log check is purely about loudness.
issues.suggested_fix: Assert on the data the log must carry rather than the wording: `assert any(rec.levelno == logging.INFO and _ESD_U1 in rec.getMessage() and '2026-01-02' in rec.getMessage() for rec in caplog.records)`. The caplog level+logger scoping already isolates the record, and entity_uuid + expires_at are the two facts an operator actually needs from that line.

issues.description: The new rationale block justifying the removal of 'count'/'topic'/'scope'/'broad' asserts that each "matches live flag_types" and names three: `recon_stale_task_count_snapshot`, `scope_violation`, `consolidated_scope_correction`. None of the three is a recon flag_type in this repo. `recon_stale_task_count_snapshot` does not exist as an identifier at all (the nearest real symbol is `harness.py::_maybe_escalate_stale_task_count_snapshot`, an escalation trigger; the gate is `flag_dedup.filter_stale_count_snapshot_corrections`). `scope_violation` is an escalation CATEGORY (`middleware/scope_violation_escalator.py:117::_CATEGORY`, also `reconciliation/targeted.py:1618`). `consolidated_scope_correction` is a `metadata.source` value (`memory_metadata.py:537`). The block then closes with 'Add a stem only after checking it against the live flag_type vocabulary' — but flag_type is free-form LLM output from the Stage-1 prompt, with only a handful of prescribed literals and no enumerable vocabulary to check against. The DECISION is right (generic single-word stems are unsafe against free-form flag_type text); only the justification is uncheckable, and the same three names are repeated in the new test docstring, which hedges them as 'real (or realistic)'.
issues.suggested_fix: Restate the rationale on the ground that actually holds: flag_type is free-form Stage-1 LLM text, so a stem that is a common English word ('count', 'scope', 'topic', 'broad') will match findings of an unrelated class and — for an entity under an active decision — silently drop them. Drop the three identifier citations (or mark them explicitly as hypothetical flag_type spellings rather than live ones), and replace the closing instruction with something executable, e.g. 'a stem must not be a standalone English word; prefer a bound morpheme like conflat/sprawl/monolith'.

verdict.summary: All six in-scope prior suggestions were genuinely addressed, and the seventh (the `escalation/models.py` prose vocabulary list) was skipped with a defensible rationale — the file is outside the task's locks, and the in-scope half was done properly by single-sourcing the category as `standing_decision_constants.CATEGORY_STANDING_DECISION_STORM`, imported by both the filer and the `DedupeConfig.infra_dedupe_categories` fold gate, so filer/reader spelling can no longer drift. I verified each fix against the real dependencies rather than the commit message: `_index_active_standing_decisions` now drops an ambiguous entity loudly (the fail-open analogue of `get_active_entity_standing_decision`'s ValueError) and skips lapsed-TTL rows using the same lexicographic string compare `ReconLedgerStore.gc()` uses, against a `now` default (`datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()`) that byte-matches the format `standing_decision_writer.py:404` writes `expires_at` in; the storm escape now folds through `escalation.dedupe.submit_or_dedupe` with an unbounded window and `content_fingerprint_key`, which I confirmed against `find_dedupe_parent`'s category/level/key/window semantics — the fingerprint includes `project_id` so the cross-project shared queue cannot mis-fold, and `make_id`'s per-key counter means the child id never collides with the parent's; the `entity_standing_decision_suppressed` pre-init is now above the remediation early return with no intervening `report.stats` reassignment; and the storm tests now drive a real `EscalationQueue`, pinning `esc.task_id`, `dedupe_fingerprint`, `dedupe_count == 1` on recurrence, the submit-raises arm, and two entities storming in one cycle. All 56 touched tests pass, and ruff + pyright are clean on the changed files. The three findings below are all new, all non-blocking, and all small: one robustness gap where the enlarged index-build raise surface now sits outside the filter's own fail-open try, one test that pins a single word of log prose where the sibling test correctly pins data, and one rationale comment whose three cited "live flag_types" are respectively nonexistent, an escalation category, and a metadata source value.
